editorial.headline: Training the People Who Keep Aviation Moving
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers private aviation education, from pilots and instructors to the personnel who support airports, navigation and security.
editorial.body:
Private providers operating under this activity deliver education and training for aviation personnel. Its scope reaches across aircraft personnel, airport personnel, air-navigation personnel and aviation-security personnel, while also including specialised transport for aircraft crews when it forms part of their education. It specifically includes education and/or training for pilots and flight instructors. In practical terms, this is an education activity built around the people whose work supports aviation operations, rather than a general-purpose classroom category.

The record also gives particular attention to institutions that provide education and/or training for airport personnel. That matters because the category is defined by the people being trained: flight-facing professionals, airport staff, navigation personnel and aviation-security personnel all sit within its stated scope. A provider should therefore present the activity as aviation-personnel education and training, with any specialised crew transport understood as part of that educational setting.

The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is a clear position: foreign participation is permitted up to full ownership at the national level. The code does not need an implied local ownership limit where the record provides none; its national setting is expressly open.

Bali does not reverse that national position for PMA registration. The province’s moratorium blocks PMA for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities island-wide and permanently, but this activity is recorded as not blocked. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—which places it outside the moratorium’s stated Low and Medium-Low reach. The Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: not a claim that aviation training is free of operational complexity, but a precise statement that this activity is not barred from PMA registration by that moratorium. For a foreign-backed provider considering Bali, the honest conclusion is straightforward: the national 100% ceiling remains meaningful here, and the Bali moratorium does not block this activity.
editorial.pullQuote: The Bali moratorium does not block this activity from PMA registration.
